corrections: Two claims I had to withdraw while writing this. (1) I believed I had edited train.py during the stage-1 startup gate. The edits are 029c43a at 19:48:58; the launch is d86bfc2 at 20:42:50, 54 minutes later, and the train.py blob has not changed since 19:48. Nothing was edited during the gate. The gap is still real and worth naming: nothing in the repo would have stopped it. pre-commit reads no running-run state, check_pod_drift SKIPs on a dev checkout, and the freeze lives in fb's order and a sentence in this file. (2) I had written that the eval scripts store gen[-300:], repeating the comment rather than checking; three of five store the full text and two did not. (3) I told fb the 3.24B milestone was ~1.5 h out; it is 22:36, four minutes off fb's independent estimate. (4) I proposed retracting the 6.6% and 25.4% base-code figures on fb's order and then found the premise was false: degeneration_rate applies [-300:] itself, so a tail-only artifact is idempotent for that metric and five of six figures recompute exactly. The sixth, L1 3-shot, is genuinely gone and is retracted as be.l1_3shot_retracted. Checking the premise before executing is what found the real defect; executing the order as given would have voided three good numbers and missed the broken one.
note: Amended six times. Ten incidents plus two named classes. Dominant root: acting on a model I constructed instead of on the system. Second class, four instances: tests that pass for a reason unrelated to their claim. t27-3 deferred to 09-01; l1 on 16281 queued behind de and tilerl.
self_assessment: Ten incidents, seven caused by me, and of those seven six were found by fb or de rather than by me. The one I caught myself was the broken kill fix, and only because I ran it against a live job instead of trusting the test I had just written. My error detection tonight was almost entirely external: everything I landed was reviewed into correctness by someone else noticing first. fb's reading is that this is the review mechanism working rather than a verdict on one session, and the mitigation is already in the row -- run the thing against the live world before reporting it. The two incidents that cost other sessions the most time (the 19s estimate, the phantom merge drop) were both cases where I reported a conclusion before testing it against anything outside my own model.
class_tests_that_pass_vacuously: FOUR tests tonight passed for a reason unrelated to what they claimed, and I wrote three of them. (1) _selftest_gpu_descendants passed on a broken _gpu_descendants because I built its ppid map from the same wrong model of the process tree the code had. (2) The first merge_complete broken world used an invented path and the selftest's own meta-check rejected it -- that one was caught by an existing guard rather than by me. (3) The first entrypoint_help check PASSED its own broken world, because a regex missed the implicit string concatenation these help strings are written with, so it read only the fragment without the percent. (4) A sync selftest dropped the LAST LINE of the real ledger to simulate a lost row; that worked only while the line's (name, started) was unique, and my closing p02_fp32m_s0 gave it a sibling event, so the identity survived the drop and the assert silently stopped firing -- it had been testing the fixture, and my own data change is what exposed it. The common shape: a test built from the same assumption as the code, or from an accident of the data, cannot falsify the thing it names. The three detections were a dry run against a live job, an existing meta-check, and a full selftest run after an unrelated commit -- none was reading the test. What I do differently: a new test must be run against a world where it MUST fail before it is trusted, and a test whose fixture is real repo data must construct the property it asserts rather than borrow it from whatever the data happens to look like today.

class_removed: A measurement or a file treated as regime-independent. Three of the four incidents have this shape: a rate measured single-stream and used to size a 7-rank load, a file that syncs one way and was written to on the read side, a baseline read as complete when it was partial. Landed: the startup gate is derived from mix cache bytes instead of a carried number. Next: --dry refuses a launch whose caches are cold. Second class, from the two later incidents: a measurement whose INSTRUMENT is wrong rather than whose arithmetic is wrong -- a liveness probe that passes on corpses, and a log line read as counting something it does not count. Both produced confident wrong answers that no amount of re-checking the arithmetic would have caught, because the arithmetic was right about the wrong quantity. Third instance of the instrument class, and the cheapest to prevent: a monitor filter that matched no process. os.kill(pid,0) passed on corpses, 'need 25' counted the wrong quantity, and this one waited on a signal that could not arrive. In all three the code ran correctly and measured nothing. Fourth class, and the inverse of the usual one (b0's framing): not a stale comment but a CORRECT comment with weaker code beneath it. The instrument class was about measurements that could not detect what they were written for; this is about prose that documents a guarantee the code does not provide. Both are invisible to the author for the same reason -- reading your own artifact confirms the intent you already hold.

incidents.evidence: commit 2f97e4a is the only record: no experiments row, no lesson entry, no retro row until this one. AGENTS.md:57 carries the lane rule; runs/tasks.jsonl t12 is check_lane_respected, which detects occupancy after the fact.
incidents.root_cause: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is not additive: an assignment in a child replaces the parent's restriction instead of indexing into it, so any physical index escapes the lane the caller set.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: landed: eval/_devs.sh is the one shard-to-card map; six scripts source it; harness check device_set_honoured walks every .sh for the class; _selftest_devs_map asserts the runtime mapping.
incidents.differently: Fix a class with a check, not five hand-edits. 2f97e4a edited three scripts by hand and both survivals below came out of that.

incidents.what: 2f97e4a's own fix still spilled. ${_DEVS[$i]:-$i} falls back to a physical index whenever the shard count exceeds the caller's card count, so CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 with eval_hard.sh's default N=6 maps shard 0 to card 7 and shards 1-5 to physical 1-5, five training-block cards.
incidents.caused_or_missed: missed by everyone for nine hours; found tonight while writing the check
incidents.evidence: reproduced against the pre-fix helper: _DEVS = 7 1 2 3 4 5. scripts/harness.py _selftest_devs_map asserts CVD=7 N=6 refuses; the old idiom fails that assert with exactly that array.
incidents.root_cause: The fallback was written for the unset-caller case and fires for the too-few-cards case as well. Two situations reach one branch and only one of them is safe.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: landed: _devs.sh refuses a shard with no card to land on and names the count. An unset caller still gets the physical first N.
incidents.differently: A default that covers two situations needs them separated before the default is written.

incidents.what: eval_all.sh kept two bare CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 assignments for nine hours after 2f97e4a fixed its three callees. It is the top-level driver, so CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 eval/eval_all.sh still put the MC suite and the FoNE probe on physical GPU 0.
incidents.caused_or_missed: missed; found tonight by the grep the check is built on
incidents.evidence: eval/eval_all.sh, both lines now source eval/_devs.sh. scripts/harness.py _broken_device_set_honoured reverts line 54 and the check FAILs on it.
incidents.root_cause: The fix was scoped to the three scripts named in the incident report rather than to the pattern, and the driver that calls them was not in that list.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: landed with the check above, which walks every .sh in the tree.
incidents.differently: After fixing an instance, grep the whole tree for the pattern before closing.

incidents.what: I read `step 130/419 loss 1.288 19s` as 19 seconds per step and told fb the v3 SFT would take 2.3 h. The field is seconds per 10 logged steps (sft_math.py:235 resets t0 each log line), so the real answer was ~9 min. v2 had printed the same 20-23s and finished 419 steps in 15 min.
incidents.caused_or_missed: caused, caught by fb before anything was scheduled on the wrong number
incidents.evidence: sft_math.py:235 prints time.time()-t0 with t0 reset at :236, one log line per 10 steps; v2's 13:32 start and 13:47 checkpoint bound it at 15 min for 419 steps
incidents.root_cause: I turned a log field into a duration without reading what the field counts. The log line names neither the unit nor the interval, so nothing contradicted me.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: proposed, not written: the log line should carry its interval (`19s/10steps`), which is a one-line change in a file frozen until the stage-1 run passes step 1000. Queued.
incidents.differently: Before a log number becomes an estimate, read the line that prints it. This is the same class as the ratio errors in docs/standards/0830v1_gates.md:844: a bare number does not carry its denominator.

incidents.what: score_matrix's degeneration metric truncates each generation to gen[-300:] and the comment justified it as 'the eval scripts store gen[-300:]'. Three of the five scorers have stored the full text since 89e7f9d; code_500 preds run to 1020 characters. The metric was discarding data already on disk and citing the disk as the reason.
incidents.caused_or_missed: caused; I wrote the CJK half of that block tonight and carried the stale claim forward
incidents.evidence: eval/score_matrix.py DEGEN_CONFIG. Measured on p324 preds: whitespace code_500 58.2% tail vs 58.8% full, math_500 2.4%/2.4%, code_500_v2 81.4%/81.4%, every CJK field unchanged. Two scorers were still truncating: eval/code_fewshot.py:163 and eval/l1_fewshot.py:114, which 89e7f9d missed.
incidents.landed_or_proposed: landed: both remaining scorers now store the full generation; the comment states the real reason and carries the measured cost; facts/base_eval.json#be.degeneration_rate no longer cites the stale code_zh.py:128. The window itself stays at 300 chars because widening it changes recorded numbers, which is fb's call. The 6.6% and 25.4% base-code figures rest on tail-only files and need a rerun to become re-derivable.
incidents.differently: A comment asserting a fact about another file is a claim to verify, not context to inherit.

class_removed: landed: physical-index device assignments. eval/_devs.sh is the single shard-to-card map, six scripts source it, harness check device_set_honoured greps every .sh for the class, and _selftest_devs_map proves the runtime mapping refuses the incident command (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 with N=6). The pre-fix idiom fails that assert, so the check has its failing case.
corrections: Two claims I had to withdraw while writing this. (1) I believed I had edited train.py during the stage-1 startup gate. The edits are 029c43a at 19:48:58; the launch is d86bfc2 at 20:42:50, 54 minutes later, and the train.py blob has not changed since 19:48. Nothing was edited during the gate. The gap is still real and worth naming: nothing in the repo would have stopped it. pre-commit reads no running-run state, check_pod_drift SKIPs on a dev checkout, and the freeze lives in fb's order and a sentence in this file. (2) I had written that the eval scripts store gen[-300:], repeating the comment rather than checking; three of five store the full text and two did not.
note: Written while pretrain_15b_s1 runs at step 450, loss 2.562, 77K tok/s/GPU, MFU 32%, ETA 7.5h. No train.py change; t27-3 stays deferred to 2026-09-01.
